crossRefs.note: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him with her sons, kneeling and asking a certain thing of him.
For they bind heavy burdens that are grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will…
But they were silent, for they had disputed with one another on the way about who was the greatest.
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came near to him, saying, “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we will ask.”
A dispute also arose among them, which of them was considered to be greatest.
In love of the brothers be tenderly affectionate to one another; in honor preferring one another;
doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
For the overseer must be blameless, as God’s steward, not self-pleasing, not easily angered, not given to wine, not…
We therefore ought to receive such, that we may be fellow workers for the truth.
He who receives you receives me, and he who receives me receives him who sent me.
“Whoever receives one such little child in my name, receives me, and whoever receives me, doesn’t receive me, but him…
and said to them, “Whoever receives this little child in my name receives me. Whoever receives me receives him who sent…

translations.web: I wrote to the assembly, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them, doesn’t accept what we say.
translations.bsb: I have written to the church about this, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first, will not accept our instruction.
translations.kjv: I wrote unto the church: but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.
translations.asv: I wrote somewhat unto the church: but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.
